preamble.description: A countersigned attestation protocol for Cardano governance actors. An attestation is issued as pending by its author and becomes a permanent record only once its subject accepts it, so no claim can be attached to an identity without that identity's own on-chain consent. Authority is carried by CIP-68 user tokens rather than signature lists, which lets an organisation or a committee acting through a script be a first-class issuer. A record can also be contested: a dispute is a separate UTxO pointing at an attestation, backed by a refundable deposit, and the attestation it contests is never hidden or deleted — the dispute is shown beside it. Four validators plus a configuration oracle: Minting Policy (token creation), Profiles Validator (profile lifecycle), Attestations Validator (acceptance and cleanup), Disputes Validator (verdict and deposit return), Oracle Validator (pause, fees, minimum UTxO, dispute deposit, admin key).
preamble.title: Palmares

datum.description: CIP-68 datum carrying the attestation: its id, the subject it is about, the issuer that authored it, its kind (one of MilestoneDelivered, AuditPassed, Affiliation, RoleHeld, Endorsement, CredentialClaim, CredentialWithdrawal), the date it was ISSUED, an optional CLAIMED PERIOD, an optional CREDENTIAL, the oracle token that authenticates the pause gate on acceptance, and whether the subject has accepted. The two dates are not the same kind of fact and a consumer must not present them alike: the issuance date is bounded by the transaction's validity interval and is therefore chain-attested within hours, while the claimed period is whatever the issuer asserted and the subject counter-signed. The kind is mostly presentational — it says what a reader is being told — with ONE exception the protocol does enforce: the two credential kinds must name a credential and must be self-issued, and the other five must name none, so a binding cannot be smuggled onto a milestone where nothing would check it.
datum.title: Attestation Datum

validators.description: Holds attestation tokens and enforces the second half of the two-phase protocol: an attestation minted as pending becomes permanent only when its subject spends it with the acceptance redeemer, which requires the subject's user token. That requirement is the whole anti-spam property — a claim cannot enter the record unilaterally. Also carries the permissionless cleanup path for dust.

redeemer.description: AcceptAttestation outputIdx — the subject accepts, flipping the acceptance flag and returning the token to this validator. The transaction must reference the oracle UTxO named by the attestation's own oracleToken, because acceptance is refused while the protocol is paused: it is the record's one irreversible write, so it is the one the pause lever must reach. Cleanup — permissionless dust removal for UTxOs whose datum is absent, does not parse, or names a state NFT the UTxO's own value does not hold.
redeemer.title: Attestations Redeemer

validators.title: Palmares Attestations Validator

datum.description: CIP-68 datum carrying the dispute: its id, the attestation it contests, the profile that opened it, when it was opened, the deposit AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID and the address it returns to, the oracle token used to authenticate the verdict, the STALE-AFTER instant past which anyone may expire it, and the verdict once set. The deposit amount is recorded here rather than read from the oracle at resolution time, so that repricing the deposit cannot change what an open dispute is owed; the deadline is recorded for the same reason, so that retiming the timeout cannot move the deadline of a dispute already open.
datum.title: Dispute Datum

validators.description: Holds a dispute and the deposit behind it. A dispute is a SEPARATE UTxO pointing at an attestation — never a field on one — so it can be opened without the subject's or the issuer's cooperation, the attestation it contests is never modified, and the attestation path's execution cost is unchanged. The oracle's ARBITER credential writes the verdict — a separate field from the admin, so verdict-writing and repricing need not be the same key — read through the oracle token recorded in the dispute's own datum so a forged oracle UTxO cannot be substituted; a verdict is written once and cannot be rewritten. The deposit returns to the address the disputer named, on EITHER verdict: there is no punitive outcome, so losing a dispute costs only network fees. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ENFORCE: one open dispute per attestation at a time. That would require an index UTxO every dispute had to contend for; what bounds dispute spam is the deposit, since each dispute is its own UTxO with its own deposit. A client that needs the uniqueness property must check it itself and must not present it as a protocol guarantee.

redeemer.description: ResolveDispute verdict outputIdx — the oracle's arbiter records VerdictUpheld or VerdictRejected, the dispute returns to this address with the verdict written and its deposit released, and the deposit is paid to the address in the datum. A resolution may NOT name VerdictExpired: that constructor is the clock's, not a decision. ExpireDispute outputIdx — after the dispute's own staleAfter deadline, ANYONE may close an undecided dispute as VerdictExpired, with no signature and no oracle read, and the deposit returns by the same rule as a resolution. It is the protocol's only permissionless state transition and it exists so that a deposit does not depend on the arbiter staying available. Cleanup — permissionless dust removal for UTxOs whose datum does not parse as protocol state, or names a dispute NFT the UTxO's own value does not hold; it fails only when that NFT is actually there.
redeemer.title: Disputes Redeemer

validators.title: Palmares Disputes Validator

validators.description: The single minting authority for protocol tokens. Parameterised by ProtocolParams (the Profiles and Attestations validator script hashes plus the oracle token), which is how validators authenticate each other. Every minting transaction reads the oracle UTxO as a reference input and is refused while the protocol is paused. Token names are derived deterministically from a seed TxOutRef, which must be spent in the same transaction, so a name cannot be replayed. The full minted value is constrained, not just the expected token name, which is what closes the other-token-name attack. THIS ENTRY PUBLISHES NO compiledCode AND NO hash, and the omission is deliberate: the policy is applied to ProtocolParams at deployment, the oracle token inside them does not exist until the one-shot oracle NFT is minted, so every deployment has a different policy hash and no single hash is true of all of them. Apply the deployment's ProtocolParams (published in the deployed-validators config) to the policy and hash the result; a hash printed here could only be a placeholder's.

parameters.description: Compile-time parameters: the Profiles, Attestations and Disputes validator script hashes, and the oracle token's AssetClass. The three script hashes are the same in every deployment — those validators are unparameterised and their compiledCode is published in this document. The oracle token is not: it is the AssetClass of the one-shot NFT minted when the protocol is deployed, which is why this validator is declared by parameter instead of shipped as code.
parameters.title: Protocol Parameters

redeemer.description: MintProfile seedTxOutRef kind metadata outputIdx — mints the CIP-68 reference and user token pair for a profile, the reference token locked at the Profiles Validator and the user token sent wherever the builder chooses, since it is the authority the holder spends to act as that profile. Minting a profile claims no credential: a binding is a CredentialClaim attestation, which is a second transaction and an append-only record. NewAttestation seedTxOutRef metadata otherMetadata subject issuer kind date claimedPeriod claimedCredential outputIdx — mints a pending attestation reference token under CIP-67 PRIVATE-USE LABEL 1, deliberately not CIP-68's label 100: an attestation has no user token, so it is not a CIP-68 pair and must not claim to be one. The label is also what lets the policy TYPE an id — the subject and the issuer must both be profile ids, so an attestation about another attestation is refused rather than minted into a record nobody could ever accept. The record is locked at the Attestations Validator. Requires the issuer's user token to be spent, refuses a self-issued record unless it is a credential binding, validates the DATE against the transaction validity range, and pays the attestation fee when the oracle configures one. The CLAIMED PERIOD is carried through unchecked and is self-reported: no on-chain fact can establish when an affiliation or a mandate began, so the protocol does not pretend to establish it. What makes a claimed period part of the record is the subject's acceptance, not a validator rule. The CLAIMED CREDENTIAL is the opposite of self-reported: it is present exactly for the two credential kinds, where the credential must prove control of this transaction and the record must be self-issued, and must be absent for the other five. OpenDispute seedTxOutRef target openedBy depositTo metadata openedAt outputIdx — mints a dispute token locked at the Disputes Validator together with the oracle's current dispute deposit, which the dispute's datum then records. Requires the disputer's own user token, and does NOT touch the attestation being contested: that is what lets anyone holding a profile contest a record without the subject's or the issuer's cooperation. Opening a dispute carries no protocol fee — the refundable deposit is the only cost that bounds it.
redeemer.title: Minting Redeemer

validators.title: Palmares Minting Policy

datum.description: Inline datum with the operational parameters: the ADMIN CREDENTIAL, the pause flag, the minimum UTxO value, the dispute deposit charged to NEW disputes, the dispute timeout in milliseconds that fixes a new dispute's stale-after deadline, an optional fee configuration (fee address plus per-action amounts), and the ARBITER CREDENTIAL. Both are credentials rather than key hashes, so a key and a native multisig are equally expressible and moving from one to the other is a rotation rather than a redeployment; a key proves control by signing, a script by spending a UTxO at its own address. The admin sets parameters; the arbiter alone writes dispute verdicts. They are the same credential at deployment and may be split later. Every update is checked for well-formedness on chain: the three amounts may not be negative and the timeout may not be zero, since a dispute whose window is empty is expirable the block after it opens. Nothing is checked about either credential — any 28 bytes are a possible hash, and whether anyone controls them is proved at rotation, not here.
datum.title: Oracle Params Datum

validators.description: Unparameterised spending validator guarding the oracle UTxO that holds OracleParams. The admin credential named by the current datum must prove control of itself on each update, and the UTxO must return to the same address with at least the same value; only the datum may change. This is how the protocol is paused, repriced (fees, minimum UTxO, and the dispute deposit for NEW disputes — an open dispute's deposit is recorded in its own datum and cannot be changed from here) or re-keyed without redeploying a validator. Re-keying is OracleSetAdmin for the admin and OracleSetArbiter for the arbiter, and BOTH SIDES must prove control: the outgoing one authorises, the incoming one proves it exists and is held, so a handover to a credential nobody controls cannot be made by mistake. A credential still controlled is recoverable by handing it on; one already lost is not, because the rotation needs its proof.

redeemer.description: OracleUpdate outputIdx action — the output index the oracle UTxO must return to, and the admin action to apply. The validator computes the expected new datum on-chain with applyOracleAdminAction and checks the output at that index against it, so off-chain and on-chain cannot disagree about the result of an update.
redeemer.title: Oracle Redeemer

validators.title: Palmares Oracle Validator

datum.description: CIP-68 datum carrying the profile: its id, its type, and the protocol parameters used to resolve sibling validator addresses. The CIP-68 shape is what makes the profile legible to wallets and marketplaces.
datum.title: Profile Datum

validators.description: Governs the profile lifecycle. Profile metadata (description and image) can be updated by whoever holds the profile's user token; the name is immutable after minting. Deletion is intentionally unsupported: a profile is the anchor of an attestation history, and that history must not become unresolvable. Unparameterised — it reads the validator addresses it needs from the datum's protocolParams.

redeemer.description: UpdateProfile newMetadataFields outputIdx — updates the mutable metadata fields with size validation, requiring the profile's user token. Cleanup — permissionless removal of a UTxO at this address whose datum is absent, does not parse, or is not backed by the state NFT it names; it fails only when the UTxO's own value holds that NFT, so legitimate state cannot be swept.
redeemer.title: Profiles Redeemer

validators.title: Palmares Profiles Validator
